final_prompt:
I want a personal habit tracker running on my machine today. It's just for me: no accounts, no login, no server. This is an MVP, so build the thinnest working slice. Throwaway structure is fine, so don't build abstractions, and don't write tests, because I want it running today.

Where to build: the current working directory is a new empty folder. Build everything here and don't touch anything outside it.

Stack: a web app that runs locally in the browser, with all data in localStorage. It must be TypeScript, not plain JavaScript. Pick the simplest TypeScript setup that works (for example Vite with the vanilla-ts template and no UI framework, unless you have a simpler option). Say in one or two sentences why you chose it. Run it with the dev server only; there's no deployment.

Look and feel: dark mode by default, with minimal clean styling in plain CSS. Don't add a light-mode toggle or a UI library.

v1 features:
- [ ] Add, edit and delete habits.
- [ ] A daily check-off: a "done today" toggle per habit.
- [ ] A streak counter per habit. A streak is the number of consecutive days checked off, ending today, or ending yesterday if today isn't checked yet. This is my assumption, so tell me if you read it differently.
- [ ] A simple 30-day history view per habit, showing the last 30 days as done or not done. It is not a full calendar.

Out of scope, so don't build or stub any of it: reminders or notifications; stats or charts; a full calendar view; accounts or login; a server or sync; a light-mode toggle; tests.

How to verify: run the dev server and confirm in the running app that you can add a few habits, check one off, reload the page and see it persist, and see the streak and 30-day history update. Also run the TypeScript type check or build and make sure it passes. In your final message, give the commands you ran and what you saw, not just "it works". If something doesn't work, fix the cause rather than hiding the error.

When to ask and when to decide: ask me only if something blocks you or would change the scope. Otherwise decide, keep going, and note the decision in your final message. Local, reversible work needs no confirmation. Ask before deleting anything outside this folder, which you shouldn't need to do.

Send a one-line note before you start and a short recap at the end, with the command to start the app and anything you decided on my behalf.

You're done when the app runs locally via the dev server, all four v1 features work in the browser, data survives a reload, the type check passes, and you've told me the start command.

I'm running this as a deep interview, so I'll go in rounds. This is round 1 of up to 4. Each question has a suggested answer in brackets, with the reason.

**1. Speed: how polished should the first version be?**
1. [MVP: the thinnest working slice, no tests. Suggested because you said you're unsure of the details, so a quick version lets you see it and react.]
2. Solid v1: tests for core logic, error handling, clean structure.

**2. Stack: what should it be built with?**
1. [Small web app: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with data in the browser's localStorage. Suggested because a personal tracker needs few screens and no server, and one session can scaffold it.]
2. Web app with React and Vite, still with local data.
3. Mobile app (React Native or Expo).
4. Your call: the simplest stack that works, with the reason explained.

**3. Features: which should v1 include? Pick any.**
a. [Add, edit and delete habits]
b. [Daily check-off, a "done today" toggle]
c. [Streak counter for each habit]
d. Calendar or heatmap history
e. Reminders or notifications
f. Weekly or monthly stats and charts

Suggested: a, b and c, because they're the minimum that makes a tracker usable. Anything you don't pick goes in the out-of-scope list.

**4. Users and data: who is it for?**
1. [Just you, with data stored locally and no accounts. Suggested because you didn't mention other users.]
2. Accounts and a server, so data syncs across devices or people.

Reply with numbers and changes, "ok" to accept all suggestions, or tell me more about what you're unsure of and I'll explain the trade-offs.

1. MVP, yes. I want something running today, and no tests.

2. Web app running locally in the browser, with data in localStorage. But I prefer TypeScript, so not plain JavaScript. Pick whatever simple setup works with TypeScript.

3. I want a, b and c, plus a simple 30-day history for each habit (d, but just the 30-day view, not a full calendar). No reminders or notifications, and no stats or charts.

4. Option 1: just me, no accounts or login, data stored locally.

One more thing: dark mode by default.

Thanks, that settles speed, stack, features and data. Round 2 covers the remaining slots.

2. Same as 1, plus the agent confirms the app builds without type errors.
3. Your own check.

**6. Existing code: where should it be built?**
1. [A new empty folder, with nothing else touched. Suggested because you didn't name a repo.]
2. Inside an existing repo. Tell me which one and what to leave alone.

**7. Look and feel: anything beyond dark mode by default?**
1. [Nothing else. Clean, minimal styling, with no UI library and no light-mode toggle. Suggested for a quick MVP.]
2. Dark by default, plus a light/dark toggle.
3. Dark by default, plus basic accessibility (keyboard-usable, readable contrast).
4. Your own styling notes.

**8. Deploy: where should it run?**
1. [Local only, using the dev server. Suggested because you said "running locally in the browser".]
2. Also deployed somewhere (for example a static host). Tell me where.

Reply with numbers and changes, or "ok" to accept all suggestions.

5. Option 1 is fine. Run it locally, add a few habits, check one off, reload and confirm it persisted, and see the streak and 30-day history update.

6. New empty folder is fine.

7. Nothing else beyond dark mode by default. Option 1 is fine.

8. Local only, dev server.
